title: Bumrah Included, Yash Thakur Replaces Harshit Rana in India T20I Squads
excerpt: The BCCI on Thursday named Vidarbha pacer Yash Thakur as Harshit Rana's replacement for the Afghanistan T20Is and the 2026 Asian Games after Rana suffered a rectus femoris strain during a match simulation, while Jasprit Bumrah, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar all made the cut.
body:
• The BCCI's men's selection committee has named Yash Thakur as the replacement for the injured Harshit Rana in India's squads for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan and the 2026 Asian Games.
  • Rana, who was rehabbing a right hamstring injury at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, sustained a rectus femoris strain while bowling during a match simulation on September 7, according to a BCCI release.
  • Jasprit Bumrah, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar — all of whom had been named in the original squad subject to fitness clearance — are included in the updated squads.
  • The T20I series against Afghanistan begins September 13 in Delhi; India's Asian Games cricket campaign starts later in September in Nagoya, Japan.

Rana's rehab setback forces a late change

The BCCI's men's selection committee on Thursday named Yash Thakur as the replacement for Harshit Rana in India's squads for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan and the cricket competition at the 2026 Asian Games. The announcement came in a BCCI media advisory issued on September 10.

Rana had first suffered an injury to his right hamstring that kept him out of action for two months, and was rehabbing at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru. According to the BCCI release, the fast bowler "was progressing well during his rehab" but "sustained a rectus femoris strain while bowling during a match simulation on September 7 and has subsequently been ruled out."

The injury is a cruel blow for Rana, whose international career has been stop-start. He missed India's last two T20Is and the ODI series in the UK, and then sat out the tour of Zimbabwe. He was named in the original squad for the Afghanistan games — but like Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Jasprit Bumrah, only subject to fitness clearance. ESPN Cricinfo reported that Reddy is now expected to get the CoE's go-ahead, and Reddy and Washington have been cleared for the series.

Who is Yash Thakur

Thakur, 27, is a right-arm fast-medium bowler from Vidarbha who made his T20I debut during India's tour of Zimbabwe in July, playing two matches and taking two wickets in each. He has built a strong domestic record: 81 wickets in 50 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy matches at an economy rate of 7.04, including 18 wickets in seven matches last season, according to MyKhel.

He has also been in recent red-ball rhythm, featuring for Central Zone in the Duleep Trophy semi-final against East Zone, where he dismissed Ishan Kishan in the first innings and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in the second. In the Indian Premier League, Thakur has played 22 matches and taken 27 wickets — he debuted in 2023 with the Lucknow Super Giants before being acquired by the Punjab Kings for Rs 1.60 crore, according to ANI.

The call-up rewards a bowler the selectors have clearly been watching. India A exposure earlier this year and the Zimbabwe tour gave Thakur a taste of the international setup; the Afghanistan series now offers him a genuine chance to establish himself.

Bumrah back, and what it means

The more consequential news for India's long-term plans may be the fitness verdicts. Bumrah, Reddy and Washington — each named in the original squad only conditionally — all appear in the updated list. That gives India a full-strength pace arsenal of Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and Thakur, backed by the spin options of Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Axar Patel and Washington.

The timing matters. India are juggling an unusually dense calendar: the three Afghanistan T20Is on September 13, 15 and 17 in Delhi, a historic one-off T20I against Japan on September 22, and then the Asian Games in Nagoya, where India are scheduled to make their first appearance on September 28, according to MyKhel. Managing Bumrah's workload through that stretch — while still giving Thakur meaningful game time — will be the management's balancing act.

"He sustained a rectus femoris strain while bowling during a match simulation on September 7 and has subsequently been ruled out."

— BCCI media release, September 10

Diaspora angle

For the Indian diaspora, the Asian Games carry a particular resonance: cricket's return to a multi-sport stage in Nagoya puts the team in front of a global audience that extends well beyond the subcontinent. With the squad led by Shreyas Iyer and featuring breakout names like Vaibhav Sooryavanshi alongside established stars, diaspora fans in the US, UK and Canada will be watching whether Thakur can convert domestic consistency into international impact.

What's next

The immediate focus is the series opener in Delhi on September 13. Watch for whether Thakur goes straight into the XI — with Bumrah's workload being managed, the new-ball combination is not yet settled. After the Afghanistan series, attention turns to the one-off Japan T20I on September 22 and then the Asian Games, where India will aim to add a cricket gold to their medal tally. Rana, meanwhile, returns to the CoE to begin another rehab — his third injury interruption of the year.

India's updated squad for Afghanistan T20Is: Shreyas Iyer (C), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson (WK), Ishan Kishan (WK), Tilak Varma (VC), Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Yash Thakur. Asian Games squad: same core 15, per the BCCI.

nri_angle: For Indian fans in the US, UK and Canada who follow the team through late-night streams and diaspora watch parties, a settled pace attack — Bumrah back, Thakur blooded — sets the tone for the home season and the Asian Games campaign in Nagoya.
